recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12399 unless Pharmacy opens a new current-version request for computable branded/unbranded or concrete/abstract medication relationships beyond the existing Medication.code coding mechanism.
issue_request: FHIR-12399 was a Published FHIR-core Medication change request with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked for Medication elements to link branded or concrete medications to unbranded or more abstract Medication resources, but the Pharmacy WG resolved to use Medication.code codings, including lower-granularity codes, rather than adding new elements.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-12399/TR 12399 source commit was found. A Jira-comment-linked Medication commit, b0500f8b520d72851aba346483f21d1ded9a86b3, applied TR 12764, TR 12394, and TR 12392 rather than this issue. The lower-granularity Medication.code wording originated in earlier FHIR-8553 guidance, was omitted during the FHIR-12391 userSelected wording update, and was restored by FHIR-13536 in commit 333047669dbe6165ff81da07eabda57b3f9880e6.
additional_context: Medication is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. The build-scoped Medication StructureDefinition has no separate unbrandedMedication or abstraction relationship element, but Medication.code currently says non-selected codings can only be literal translations or lower-granularity codes, matching the mechanism cited by the FHIR-12399 resolution. The related FHIR-13536 audit is already on the combined branch, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because adding a new Medication relationship element would contradict the final modified resolution, while adding redundant narrative would not change implementer understanding beyond the authoritative Medication.code comment already in source.
